easy.question: Where did Israel travel at the beginning of the passage?
easy.explanation: The first verse says, “And came to Beersheba.”

easy.question: Who spoke to Israel in the visions of the night?
easy.explanation: The second verse says, “And God spake unto Israel in the visions of the night.”

easy.question: What did God promise to make Israel in Egypt?
easy.explanation: God said, “For I will there make of thee a great nation.”

medium.question: What did Israel do before God spoke to him in the visions of the night?
medium.explanation: Israel first came to Beersheba and offered sacrifices; only afterward did God speak to him.

medium.question: What does “visions” mean in the phrase “the visions of the night”?
answers: Objects used to see one’s face
Revelations or visions seen in a dream
medium.explanation: Here, “visions” means revelations or visions received at night.

medium.question: Why did God tell Israel not to be afraid to go down to Egypt?
answers: Because Joseph had already left Egypt
Because God promised to make him a great nation there
medium.explanation: God reassured Israel that going to Egypt was part of His promise: “I will there make of thee a great nation.”

challenge.question: What can we understand from God calling him both “Israel” and “Jacob”?
answers: They are two names for the same person
challenge.explanation: Israel and Jacob are two names for the same patriarch, so God addresses the same person in both ways.

challenge.question: What does the promise “I will go down with thee into Egypt” teach about Israel’s journey?
answers: Israel would not have to leave Beersheba
God promised to be with Israel on the journey and in Egypt
Israel would go down to Egypt alone and without help
challenge.explanation: “I will go down with thee” means that God promised to accompany Israel and not leave him alone.

challenge.question: What is meant by the detail that Joseph would “put his hand upon thine eyes”?
answers: Joseph would help Israel see the way
Joseph would hide Egypt from Israel
Joseph would be with Israel at his death and close his eyes
challenge.explanation: Placing a hand on the eyes refers to closing the eyes of the dead; Joseph would be beside Israel until the end of his life.

questions.question: What can we understand from God calling him both “Israel” and “Jacob”?
answers: They are two names for the same person
questions.explanation: Israel and Jacob are two names for the same patriarch, so God addresses the same person in both ways.

questions.question: What does the promise “I will go down with thee into Egypt” teach about Israel’s journey?
answers: Israel would not have to leave Beersheba
God promised to be with Israel on the journey and in Egypt
Israel would go down to Egypt alone and without help
questions.explanation: “I will go down with thee” means that God promised to accompany Israel and not leave him alone.

questions.question: What is meant by the detail that Joseph would “put his hand upon thine eyes”?
answers: Joseph would help Israel see the way
Joseph would hide Egypt from Israel
Joseph would be with Israel at his death and close his eyes
questions.explanation: Placing a hand on the eyes refers to closing the eyes of the dead; Joseph would be beside Israel until the end of his life.

paragraphs.title: Jacob and His Family Go Down to Egypt

easy.question: Where did Jacob and all his descendants arrive?
easy.explanation: Verse 6 says, “And came into Egypt, Jacob, and all his seed with him.”

easy.question: Who carried Jacob, the little ones, and the women in the wagons?
easy.explanation: The sons of Israel carried Jacob, their children, and their wives in the wagons.

easy.question: What did Pharaoh send to carry Jacob?
easy.explanation: The verse says that Pharaoh sent wagons to carry Jacob.

medium.question: What was the correct order of events in these verses?
answers: Jacob rose from Beersheba, the family took their possessions, and they came into Egypt
The family came into Egypt, and afterward rose from Beersheba
Pharaoh came to Canaan, and afterward the family took their possessions
medium.explanation: First Jacob rose from Beersheba, then they took their livestock and goods, and finally they came into Egypt.

medium.question: What were the wagons sent by Pharaoh used for?
medium.explanation: The wagons were sent “to carry him,” helping transport Jacob and his family.

medium.question: What does “their goods” mean in the phrase “their goods, which they had gotten”?
medium.explanation: “Their goods” means the possessions they owned, which they had acquired in Canaan.

challenge.question: What can we infer from “all his seed” and the list of family members in verse 7?
answers: The move to Egypt included the extended family
Only Jacob’s sons moved to Egypt
Only the women moved to Egypt
challenge.explanation: The verse lists sons, grandsons, daughters, and granddaughters, showing that the extended family moved together.

challenge.question: What can we understand from their taking both their livestock and the goods acquired in Canaan?
answers: They were traveling to Egypt only briefly
They moved to Egypt with their possessions and animals
They sold all their possessions before traveling
challenge.explanation: The text emphasizes that they took their livestock and goods, so the move included their property as well as their family.

challenge.question: What important detail does the verse give about Pharaoh?
answers: Pharaoh sent wagons, but the verse does not say that he traveled with them
challenge.explanation: The verse says that Pharaoh sent the wagons; it does not say that Pharaoh himself joined the journey.

questions.question: What can we infer from “all his seed” and the list of family members in verse 7?
answers: The move to Egypt included the extended family
Only Jacob’s sons moved to Egypt
Only the women moved to Egypt
questions.explanation: The verse lists sons, grandsons, daughters, and granddaughters, showing that the extended family moved together.

questions.question: What can we understand from their taking both their livestock and the goods acquired in Canaan?
answers: They were traveling to Egypt only briefly
They moved to Egypt with their possessions and animals
They sold all their possessions before traveling
questions.explanation: The text emphasizes that they took their livestock and goods, so the move included their property as well as their family.

questions.question: What important detail does the verse give about Pharaoh?
answers: Pharaoh sent wagons, but the verse does not say that he traveled with them
questions.explanation: The verse says that Pharaoh sent the wagons; it does not say that Pharaoh himself joined the journey.

easy.question: Who was Jacob’s firstborn son?
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Reuben, Jacob’s firstborn.”

easy.question: Who was Jacob’s daughter mentioned in verse 15?
easy.explanation: Verse 15 specifically names “his daughter Dinah.”

easy.question: How many people from Leah’s sons and daughters were counted?
easy.explanation: The end of verse 15 says, “All the souls of his sons and his daughters were thirty and three.”

medium.question: Who were the sons of Pharez mentioned after Er and Onan died?
medium.explanation: After stating that Er and Onan died, the verse names Pharez’s two sons: Hezron and Hamul.

medium.question: What does “firstborn” mean in the phrase “Reuben, Jacob’s firstborn”?
medium.explanation: “Firstborn” means the first son to be born. Reuben was Jacob’s first son.

medium.question: Which group of names belongs to Levi’s sons?
medium.explanation: Verse 11 lists Levi’s sons as Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.

challenge.question: What can we infer from Hezron and Hamul being listed after Judah’s sons?
answers: The list also includes grandchildren through one of Jacob’s sons
Hezron and Hamul were Levi’s sons
Judah was the son of Hezron and Hamul
challenge.explanation: Hezron and Hamul were sons of Pharez, and Pharez was Judah’s son, so the list includes another generation.

challenge.question: What special detail is given about Shaul, one of Simeon’s sons?
answers: He was the son of a Canaanitish woman
challenge.explanation: Verse 10 specifically says, “Shaul the son of a Canaanitish woman.”

challenge.question: What can we learn from verse 15 about Leah’s connection with Jacob?
answers: Leah first met Jacob in Egypt
Leah bore children to Jacob in Padanaram
challenge.explanation: The verse says that Leah bore them to Jacob in Padanaram.

questions.question: What can we infer from Hezron and Hamul being listed after Judah’s sons?
answers: The list also includes grandchildren through one of Jacob’s sons
Hezron and Hamul were Levi’s sons
Judah was the son of Hezron and Hamul
questions.explanation: Hezron and Hamul were sons of Pharez, and Pharez was Judah’s son, so the list includes another generation.

questions.question: What special detail is given about Shaul, one of Simeon’s sons?
answers: He was the son of a Canaanitish woman
questions.explanation: Verse 10 specifically says, “Shaul the son of a Canaanitish woman.”

questions.question: What can we learn from verse 15 about Leah’s connection with Jacob?
answers: Leah first met Jacob in Egypt
Leah bore children to Jacob in Padanaram
questions.explanation: The verse says that Leah bore them to Jacob in Padanaram.

paragraphs.title: The Sons of Zilpah and the Growing Family

easy.question: Who were the sons of Gad mentioned in the verse?
answers: Ziphion, Haggi, Shuni, Ezbon, Eri, Arodi, and Areli
Jemnah, Ishuah, Isui, Beriah, Heber, and Malchiel
easy.explanation: Verse 16 lists Gad’s seven sons: Ziphion, Haggi, Shuni, Ezbon, Eri, Arodi, and Areli.

easy.question: Who was the sister of Asher’s sons?
easy.explanation: Verse 17 says, “Serah their sister.”

easy.question: How many people are attributed to Zilpah’s family?
easy.explanation: The end of verse 18 says, “Even sixteen souls.”

medium.question: Why are the people in verse 18 called “the sons of Zilpah”?
answers: Because Zilpah bore them to Jacob
Because they were born in Canaan
medium.explanation: The verse says that Zilpah bore these people to Jacob, so they are called her sons.

medium.question: What does “bare” mean in the phrase “these she bare unto Jacob”?
medium.explanation: “Bare” means gave birth to. The verse says that Zilpah bore these people to Jacob.

medium.question: Who were Heber and Malchiel?
medium.explanation: Verse 17 says, “The sons of Beriah; Heber, and Malchiel.”

challenge.question: What can we infer from the name Beriah appearing among Asher’s sons and again in “the sons of Beriah”?
answers: Beriah was the father of Heber and Malchiel
Beriah was Heber and Malchiel’s sister
Beriah was one of Gad’s sons
challenge.explanation: Beriah is first listed among Asher’s sons, and then Heber and Malchiel are identified as his sons.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that the list does not include only males?
answers: Serah is mentioned as their sister
challenge.explanation: Serah is identified as their sister, showing that a daughter is included in the list.

challenge.question: How many people are named in Zilpah’s family list, not counting Zilpah herself?
challenge.explanation: Seven sons of Gad and seven descendants of Asher are named, making fourteen people altogether.

questions.question: What can we infer from the name Beriah appearing among Asher’s sons and again in “the sons of Beriah”?
answers: Beriah was the father of Heber and Malchiel
Beriah was Heber and Malchiel’s sister
Beriah was one of Gad’s sons
questions.explanation: Beriah is first listed among Asher’s sons, and then Heber and Malchiel are identified as his sons.

questions.question: Which detail shows that the list does not include only males?
answers: Serah is mentioned as their sister
questions.explanation: Serah is identified as their sister, showing that a daughter is included in the list.

questions.question: How many people are named in Zilpah’s family list, not counting Zilpah herself?
questions.explanation: Seven sons of Gad and seven descendants of Asher are named, making fourteen people altogether.

easy.question: Who were Rachel, Jacob’s wife’s, two sons?
easy.explanation: Verse 19 says that Rachel’s sons were Joseph and Benjamin.

easy.question: Who was the mother of Manasseh and Ephraim?
easy.explanation: Verse 20 says that Asenath bore Manasseh and Ephraim to Joseph.

easy.question: How many people from Rachel’s family were counted?
easy.explanation: The end of verse 22 says, “All the souls were fourteen.”

medium.question: What was the relationship between Joseph, Manasseh, and Ephraim?
medium.explanation: Manasseh and Ephraim were born to Joseph, so they were his sons.

medium.question: What does “soul” mean in the phrase “all the souls were fourteen”?
medium.explanation: Here, “soul” means a person or family member; fourteen people from Rachel’s family were counted.

medium.question: Why were Manasseh and Ephraim included in Rachel’s family list?
answers: Because they were born to Benjamin
Because they were Rachel’s sons directly
Because they were Joseph’s sons, and Joseph was Rachel’s son
medium.explanation: Manasseh and Ephraim were Joseph’s sons, and Joseph was Rachel’s son, so they belonged to Rachel’s family.

challenge.question: Which detail explains why the final number is fourteen?
answers: Joseph, Benjamin, Joseph’s two sons, and Benjamin’s ten sons are counted
Only Benjamin’s ten sons and four women are counted
Jacob’s twelve sons and two priests are counted
challenge.explanation: The number includes Joseph and Benjamin, Manasseh and Ephraim, and Benjamin’s ten sons: fourteen in all.

challenge.question: What can we infer from Manasseh and Ephraim being born in Egypt but still included in the list?
answers: They were not connected to Jacob’s family
Their family connection was determined by their father Joseph, not by their birthplace
challenge.explanation: Although born in Egypt, they were Joseph’s sons and therefore part of Jacob’s family through their father.

challenge.question: Which detail in Benjamin’s list is especially easy to miss?
challenge.explanation: Verse 21 lists ten of Benjamin’s sons, helping produce the total of fourteen.

questions.question: Which detail explains why the final number is fourteen?
answers: Joseph, Benjamin, Joseph’s two sons, and Benjamin’s ten sons are counted
Only Benjamin’s ten sons and four women are counted
Jacob’s twelve sons and two priests are counted
questions.explanation: The number includes Joseph and Benjamin, Manasseh and Ephraim, and Benjamin’s ten sons: fourteen in all.

questions.question: What can we infer from Manasseh and Ephraim being born in Egypt but still included in the list?
answers: They were not connected to Jacob’s family
Their family connection was determined by their father Joseph, not by their birthplace
questions.explanation: Although born in Egypt, they were Joseph’s sons and therefore part of Jacob’s family through their father.

questions.question: Which detail in Benjamin’s list is especially easy to miss?
questions.explanation: Verse 21 lists ten of Benjamin’s sons, helping produce the total of fourteen.

easy.question: Who was Dan’s son?
easy.explanation: The verse says, “The sons of Dan; Hushim.”

easy.question: How many sons of Naphtali are mentioned?
easy.explanation: Four sons are mentioned: Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem.

easy.question: Who gave Bilhah to Rachel?
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Which Laban gave unto Rachel his daughter.”

medium.question: Whose sons are mentioned after Dan’s son?
medium.explanation: After Hushim, Dan’s son, the verse lists Naphtali’s sons.

medium.question: What does “soul” mean in the phrase “all the souls were seven”?
medium.explanation: In this family list, “soul” means a person; the total was seven people.

medium.question: What did Dan and Naphtali have in common according to these verses?
answers: They both gave Bilhah to Rachel
They were both sons of Bilhah and had children by Jacob
medium.explanation: Verse 25 explains that the people listed were Bilhah’s sons, and that she bore them to Jacob.

challenge.question: Why does verse 25 say, “These are the sons of Bilhah” after listing Dan’s and Naphtali’s sons?
answers: To connect the lists of Dan and Naphtali to Bilhah
To say that Bilhah was Naphtali’s daughter
To announce that Laban was Jacob’s son
challenge.explanation: The concluding verse clarifies that all the names listed were Bilhah’s sons.

challenge.question: Which comparison between the lists of Dan and Naphtali is correct?
answers: Seven sons are mentioned for each
One son is mentioned for Dan, and four for Naphtali
Four sons are mentioned for Dan, and one for Naphtali
challenge.explanation: Only Hushim is listed for Dan, while Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem are listed for Naphtali.

challenge.question: What sequence of relationships appears in the verse?
answers: Rachel gave Laban to Bilhah, and Bilhah bore Jacob
Jacob gave Bilhah to Laban, and Laban fathered Rachel
Laban gave Bilhah to Rachel, and Bilhah bore the sons to Jacob
challenge.explanation: The verse first says that Laban gave Bilhah to Rachel, and then that Bilhah bore the sons to Jacob.

questions.question: Why does verse 25 say, “These are the sons of Bilhah” after listing Dan’s and Naphtali’s sons?
answers: To connect the lists of Dan and Naphtali to Bilhah
To say that Bilhah was Naphtali’s daughter
To announce that Laban was Jacob’s son
questions.explanation: The concluding verse clarifies that all the names listed were Bilhah’s sons.

questions.question: Which comparison between the lists of Dan and Naphtali is correct?
answers: Seven sons are mentioned for each
One son is mentioned for Dan, and four for Naphtali
Four sons are mentioned for Dan, and one for Naphtali
questions.explanation: Only Hushim is listed for Dan, while Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem are listed for Naphtali.

questions.question: What sequence of relationships appears in the verse?
answers: Rachel gave Laban to Bilhah, and Bilhah bore Jacob
Jacob gave Bilhah to Laban, and Laban fathered Rachel
Laban gave Bilhah to Rachel, and Bilhah bore the sons to Jacob
questions.explanation: The verse first says that Laban gave Bilhah to Rachel, and then that Bilhah bore the sons to Jacob.

paragraphs.title: Seventy People Go Down to Egypt

easy.question: How many people from Jacob’s household came into Egypt?
easy.explanation: Verse 27 says, “All the souls of the house of Jacob, which came into Egypt, were threescore and ten,” or seventy.

easy.question: How many sons were born to Joseph in Egypt?
easy.explanation: The verse says that Joseph’s sons born in Egypt were “two souls.”

easy.question: Who was not included in the number of sixty-six?
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly says, “Besides Jacob’s sons’ wives.”

medium.question: Why were Joseph’s sons born in Egypt not included in the number sixty-six?
answers: They were born in Egypt and did not come with Jacob
medium.explanation: The number sixty-six refers to those who came with Jacob; Joseph’s sons had already been born in Egypt.

medium.question: What does the phrase “came out of his loins” mean here?
answers: People who went on a journey
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to Jacob’s descendants, the members of his family who came to Egypt.

medium.question: What order of events is described in these verses?
answers: Joseph’s sons were born in Egypt, and then Jacob’s family members who came with him were counted
Joseph left Egypt, and then his sons were born
Jacob’s wives arrived, and then Jacob was born
medium.explanation: The verses distinguish between the family members who came with Jacob and Joseph’s sons, who were already born in Egypt.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the difference between the numbers sixty-six and seventy?
answers: There is an error in the numbers
Sixty-six is only part of the group, while seventy is the total
challenge.explanation: Sixty-six refers to those who came with Jacob, while seventy is the total number of Jacob’s household given in the verse.

challenge.question: What was special about Joseph’s sons compared with the other people counted?
answers: They were born in Egypt rather than arriving from Canaan
They were the only people who came out of Jacob’s loins
challenge.explanation: The verse emphasizes that Joseph’s sons were born in Egypt, unlike those who arrived there with Jacob.

challenge.question: What does “soul” mean in these verses?
answers: A person counted among the people
challenge.explanation: “Soul” is used here to mean an individual person, so the verses count the members of the family.

questions.question: What can we infer from the difference between the numbers sixty-six and seventy?
answers: There is an error in the numbers
Sixty-six is only part of the group, while seventy is the total
questions.explanation: Sixty-six refers to those who came with Jacob, while seventy is the total number of Jacob’s household given in the verse.

questions.question: What was special about Joseph’s sons compared with the other people counted?
answers: They were born in Egypt rather than arriving from Canaan
They were the only people who came out of Jacob’s loins
questions.explanation: The verse emphasizes that Joseph’s sons were born in Egypt, unlike those who arrived there with Jacob.

questions.question: What does “soul” mean in these verses?
answers: A person counted among the people
questions.explanation: “Soul” is used here to mean an individual person, so the verses count the members of the family.

easy.question: Whom did Jacob send ahead to Joseph?
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And he sent Judah before him unto Joseph.”

easy.question: Where did Jacob and his family arrive?
easy.explanation: The family came to the land of Goshen, as the verse says.

easy.question: What did Israel say after seeing Joseph?
answers: He wanted to return to Canaan
He wanted to speak with Pharaoh
He could die peacefully after seeing that Joseph was alive
easy.explanation: Israel said, “Now let me die, since I have seen thy face, because thou art yet alive.”

medium.question: What was the correct order of events?
answers: Judah was sent ahead, the family arrived in Goshen, and Joseph met his father
Joseph met his father, then Judah was sent, and finally they arrived in Goshen
The family returned to Canaan, and then Joseph came to them
medium.explanation: First Judah was sent ahead, then the family arrived in Goshen, and afterward Joseph went to meet Israel.

medium.question: What does “to direct his face unto Goshen” mean?
answers: To guide and show the way
medium.explanation: The context shows that Judah was sent ahead to guide the family toward Goshen.

medium.question: Why did Israel say that he could die after seeing Joseph?
answers: Because he did not want to enter Egypt
Because Joseph asked him to die
Seeing Joseph alive fulfilled his joy and brought him peace
medium.explanation: Seeing Joseph alive after their long separation gave Israel great joy and peace.

challenge.question: Which action of Joseph especially expresses the strength of his emotion when he met his father?
answers: He fell on his father’s neck and wept
He stayed in his chariot and did not get down
challenge.explanation: Falling on Israel’s neck and weeping for a long time show deep emotion and love.

challenge.question: What can we infer from Joseph preparing his chariot and going to meet Israel?
answers: Joseph was afraid to reach Goshen
Joseph held a position that allowed him to use an honored chariot
Joseph did not know where his father was
challenge.explanation: The chariot was a sign of status, emphasizing Joseph’s high position in Egypt.

challenge.question: What does the word “yet” emphasize in “because thou art yet alive”?
answers: Joseph had arrived in Egypt for the first time
Joseph was still alive despite the years and separation
challenge.explanation: “Yet” means “still,” emphasizing Israel’s joy that Joseph remained alive.

questions.question: Which action of Joseph especially expresses the strength of his emotion when he met his father?
answers: He fell on his father’s neck and wept
He stayed in his chariot and did not get down
questions.explanation: Falling on Israel’s neck and weeping for a long time show deep emotion and love.

questions.question: What can we infer from Joseph preparing his chariot and going to meet Israel?
answers: Joseph was afraid to reach Goshen
Joseph held a position that allowed him to use an honored chariot
Joseph did not know where his father was
questions.explanation: The chariot was a sign of status, emphasizing Joseph’s high position in Egypt.

questions.question: What does the word “yet” emphasize in “because thou art yet alive”?
answers: Joseph had arrived in Egypt for the first time
Joseph was still alive despite the years and separation
questions.explanation: “Yet” means “still,” emphasizing Israel’s joy that Joseph remained alive.

easy.question: To whom did Joseph say he would go and speak?
easy.explanation: Joseph said that he would go to Pharaoh and tell him about his family.

easy.question: Who had come to Joseph?
answers: His brothers and his father’s household
easy.explanation: Joseph told Pharaoh that his brothers and his father’s household had come to him.

easy.question: From what land had Joseph’s brothers and his father’s household come?
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly says that they came from the land of Canaan.

medium.question: What did Joseph plan to do before telling Pharaoh about his family?
answers: Send his brothers into the wilderness
medium.explanation: Joseph said, “I will go up, and shew Pharaoh,” meaning he would first go to Pharaoh and then tell him.

medium.question: What does “I will go up” mean in this context?
medium.explanation: In context, “I will go up” means that Joseph would go or approach Pharaoh to speak with him.

medium.question: What would Joseph tell Pharaoh about his family?
answers: They had lived in Egypt for many years
They had come to him from the land of Canaan
medium.explanation: Joseph planned to say that his brothers and his father’s household had come to him from Canaan.

challenge.question: Why did Joseph emphasize his family’s land of origin to Pharaoh?
answers: To explain who they were and where they had come from
To say that they were longtime Egyptians
To announce that they were enemies of Egypt
challenge.explanation: Saying that they came from Canaan gave Pharaoh clear information about the family’s identity and origin.

challenge.question: According to the order of the verse, what would happen first?
answers: Pharaoh would ask Joseph about his family
Joseph would go up to Pharaoh
The family would return to Canaan
challenge.explanation: Joseph says first, “I will go up,” and afterward, “and shew Pharaoh.”

challenge.question: To whom does the phrase “which were in the land of Canaan” refer?
answers: Joseph’s brothers and his father’s household
challenge.explanation: The phrase describes the brothers and the father’s household, who had been in Canaan.

questions.question: Why did Joseph emphasize his family’s land of origin to Pharaoh?
answers: To explain who they were and where they had come from
To say that they were longtime Egyptians
To announce that they were enemies of Egypt
questions.explanation: Saying that they came from Canaan gave Pharaoh clear information about the family’s identity and origin.

questions.question: According to the order of the verse, what would happen first?
answers: Pharaoh would ask Joseph about his family
Joseph would go up to Pharaoh
The family would return to Canaan
questions.explanation: Joseph says first, “I will go up,” and afterward, “and shew Pharaoh.”

questions.question: To whom does the phrase “which were in the land of Canaan” refer?
answers: Joseph’s brothers and his father’s household
questions.explanation: The phrase describes the brothers and the father’s household, who had been in Canaan.

paragraphs.title: The Family and Their Possessions Arrive in Egypt

easy.question: What occupation did the men have?
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And the men are shepherds.”

easy.question: What animals did the men bring?
easy.explanation: The verse says that they brought their flocks and their herds.

easy.question: What else did the men bring besides their flocks and herds?
easy.explanation: The verse says that they brought “all that they have.”

medium.question: Why were the men called shepherds?
answers: Because they were keepers of livestock
Because they lived near the sea
medium.explanation: The verse explains that their trade was to feed or care for cattle.

medium.question: What can we understand from their bringing everything they had?
medium.explanation: “All that they have” shows that they brought their property with them.

medium.question: What does “cattle” mean in the phrase “their trade hath been to feed cattle”?
medium.explanation: The context immediately mentions flocks and herds, so “cattle” means livestock.

challenge.question: What is the function of “for” in “the men are shepherds, for their trade hath been to feed cattle”?
challenge.explanation: “For” explains why they were shepherds: their occupation was caring for livestock.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “their flocks, and their herds” emphasize?
answers: That they owned only two animals
That they bought animals in Egypt
That they possessed both flocks and herds
challenge.explanation: The phrase names two kinds of livestock that belonged to them.

challenge.question: What can we infer about the way the men traveled?
answers: They moved with their animals and possessions
They traveled alone and left everything behind
They sent only a messenger with their possessions
challenge.explanation: The verse says they brought their flocks, herds, and everything they owned, so they moved with their property.

questions.question: What is the function of “for” in “the men are shepherds, for their trade hath been to feed cattle”?
questions.explanation: “For” explains why they were shepherds: their occupation was caring for livestock.

questions.question: What does the phrase “their flocks, and their herds” emphasize?
answers: That they owned only two animals
That they bought animals in Egypt
That they possessed both flocks and herds
questions.explanation: The phrase names two kinds of livestock that belonged to them.

questions.question: What can we infer about the way the men traveled?
answers: They moved with their animals and possessions
They traveled alone and left everything behind
They sent only a messenger with their possessions
questions.explanation: The verse says they brought their flocks, herds, and everything they owned, so they moved with their property.

paragraphs.title: Preparing to Answer Pharaoh and Requesting Goshen

easy.question: What did Pharaoh ask Joseph and his brothers?
easy.explanation: Pharaoh asked, “What is your occupation?”

easy.question: What occupation did the brothers have?
easy.explanation: The brothers said that they were keepers of livestock and shepherds.

easy.question: In what land did the brothers ask to live?
easy.explanation: The brothers asked to dwell in the land of Goshen.

medium.question: Why did the brothers tell Pharaoh that they were shepherds?
answers: So that they could live in the land of Goshen
So that they could receive positions in the palace
So that they could hide their family
